headline: A huge typhoon forces a million people from their homes

sources.title: More than 1.7 million evacuated as Typhoon Bavi makes landfall in China
Typhoon Bavi makes landfall in eastern China as more than 1 million are evacuated
China evacuates over one million as Typhoon Bavi nears

chunks.text: A powerful storm called Typhoon Bavi has {{moved in}} on eastern China. Before it reached land, [[officials]] {{moved out}} more than 1.7 million people from towns near the coast in Zhejiang province. China's weather service {{put out}} an orange alert, the second-highest warning level.

verbs.correct: To come closer in a threatening way

verbs.wrong: To warn people that danger is coming
verbs.correct: To make people leave a place

verbs.wrong: To raise a warning to a higher level
verbs.correct: To produce or give out something

chunks.text: Out at sea, Bavi had {{built up}} into a huge typhoon with winds near 89 miles per hour. On its way, it {{passed by}} the Philippines and Taiwan, where the storm killed and hurt many people. Weather forecasters [[warned]] that it could {{knock down}} trees and flood streets when it reached the coastal city of Yuhuan late on Saturday night.

verbs.wrong: To move quickly across the ocean
verbs.correct: To slowly become bigger or stronger

verbs.wrong: To stop in a place for a short time
verbs.correct: To move past a place without stopping

verbs.wrong: To pull something out of the ground
verbs.correct: To hit something so it falls to the ground

chunks.text: The typhoon {{shut down}} [[normal life]] [[across the region]]. Airlines {{called off}} [[hundreds of]] flights, and fast trains and ferry services stopped for the weekend. Officials also {{set up}} shelters where families could stay safe until the danger passed.

verbs.wrong: To force people to stay in their homes
verbs.correct: To stop something from working or being open

verbs.wrong: To move something to a later date
verbs.correct: To cancel something that was planned

verbs.wrong: To pay the cost of something for other people

chunks.text: Rescue teams {{teamed up}} to [[get ready for the worst]]. In Fujian province, more than 17,000 rescue workers were {{standing by}}, [[ready to help]], and the government [[promised]] millions of dollars for relief. Officials hoped that all of this [[careful planning]] would {{pay off}} and [[keep people safe]].

verbs.correct: To join with others to work together

verbs.wrong: To promise to support a person no matter what
verbs.correct: To be ready to help or act at any moment

verbs.wrong: To happen exactly the way it was planned
verbs.correct: To bring a good result after hard work

vocab.def: To come closer in a threatening way
ex: Dark clouds moved in before the rain started.
The army moved in on the town at night.
A cold front is moving in from the north.

vocab.def: To make people leave a place
ex: Police moved out the crowd for safety.
The town moved out families before the flood.
They moved out everyone near the fire.

vocab.def: To produce or give out something
ex: The office put out a new report today.
The government put out a warning about the storm.
The company put out a short statement.

vocab.def: To slowly become bigger or stronger
ex: Traffic builds up during rush hour.
Pressure was building up before the storm.
Excitement built up before the game.

vocab.def: To move past a place without stopping
ex: The storm passed by the coast during the night.
We passed by your house on the way home.
A parade passed by the school.

vocab.def: To hit something so it falls to the ground
ex: The strong wind knocked down several trees.
The car knocked down a road sign.
Workers knocked down the old wall.

vocab.def: To stop something from working or being open
ex: The storm shut down the whole airport.
They shut down the factory for the holiday.
Bad weather shut down the roads.

vocab.def: To cancel something that was planned
ex: They called off the match because of rain.
The trip was called off at the last minute.
Officials called off the event for safety.
The city set up shelters for the storm.
They set up a new website in one day.
We set up a meeting for Monday.

vocab.def: To join with others to work together
ex: The two countries teamed up to fight the fire.
She teamed up with a friend for the project.
Doctors teamed up to help the patients.

vocab.def: To be ready to help or act at any moment
ex: Rescue teams were standing by all night.
Doctors stood by in case of an accident.
Please stand by for more news.

vocab.def: To bring a good result after hard work
ex: All her practice finally paid off.
The careful plan paid off in the end.
Their hard work paid off with a win.

wordDefs.def: People with important jobs in a government or an organization
ex: The officials checked our passports at the border.
City officials opened the new library on Monday.

wordDefs.def: Told someone about a possible danger or problem
ex: My friend warned me about the icy road.
The teacher warned us that the test would be hard.

wordDefs.def: The ordinary daily routine that people usually have
ex: After the flu, it took me a week to return to normal life.
He missed normal life while he was working abroad.

wordDefs.def: In every part of a large area
ex: Schools across the region closed because of the snow.
Farmers across the region had a very good year.
There were hundreds of people at the concert.
She has hundreds of photos on her phone.

wordDefs.def: To prepare for the worst thing that could happen
ex: We packed extra food and water to get ready for the worst.
Good drivers check their tires and get ready for the worst.

wordDefs.def: Willing and prepared to give someone assistance
ex: My neighbors are always ready to help.
The staff is ready to help if you have a question.

wordDefs.def: Said firmly that you will do something
ex: She promised to call me tonight.
He promised his sister a birthday gift.

wordDefs.def: Thinking about every detail before doing something
ex: The trip went well because of careful planning.
Their careful planning made the party a success.

wordDefs.def: To protect people from danger or harm
ex: Seat belts keep people safe in a crash.
Better street lights help keep people safe at night.

tf.s: Only a few workers were ready to help during the storm.
tf.why: More than 17,000 rescue workers were standing by in Fujian province alone.

tf.s: Airlines called off hundreds of flights because of the storm.
tf.why: The story says airlines called off hundreds of flights for the weekend.

tf.s: Typhoon Bavi reached the coast in the middle of the day on Monday.
tf.why: The storm reached the coastal city of Yuhuan late on Saturday night, not on Monday.

tf.s: The storm passed by the Philippines and Taiwan before it reached China.
tf.why: On its way, Bavi passed by the Philippines and Taiwan, where it killed and hurt many people.

tf.s: Officials moved more than 1.7 million people away from the coast in Zhejiang before the storm arrived.
tf.why: The story says officials moved out more than 1.7 million people from towns near the coast in Zhejiang province.

tf.s: Officials refused to set up shelters, so families had to stay in their own homes.
tf.why: False. Officials set up shelters where families could stay safe until the danger passed.
